bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is the 16-byte blob `17 00 D6 01 00 00 00 03 20 20 01 00 00 00 20 01`. In `fuzz_binary_decode`, the first two bytes select `UA_TYPES_VARIANT`, and `Variant_decodeBinary()` reads the remaining payload as a one-element array of `ExtensionObject`. The sole element's `NodeId` bytes decode as a string `NodeId` (`encoding 0x03`, namespaceIndex `0x2020`, string length 1, identifier byte `0x20`), so `UA_findDataTypeByBinary()` cannot resolve it to a known binary type. `ExtensionObject_decodeBinaryContent()` therefore takes the unknown-type arm and performs `dst->content.encoded.typeId = *typeId`, which aliases the heap-owned `binTypeId` string into the destination instead of copying it. The next witness byte is `0x01` (`UA_EXTENSIONOBJECT_ENCODED_BYTESTRING`), but the file ends immediately afterwards, so decoding the encoded body fails before even reading the required 4-byte body length. `ExtensionObject_decodeBinary()` still calls `UA_NodeId_deleteMembers(&binTypeId)`, freeing the aliased 1-byte string once, and the outer `Array_decodeBinary()` error cleanup immediately deletes the partially decoded `ExtensionObject`, where `ExtensionObject_deleteMembers()` -> `NodeId_deleteMembers()` -> `String_deleteMembers()` frees the same buffer again. The fixing commit changes the aliasing assignment to `UA_NodeId_copy(typeId, &dst->content.encoded.typeId);`.

source.description: First non-harness project statement on the witnessed path that turns attacker-controlled bytes into vulnerability-relevant parser state: the top-level `Variant` header selects `ExtensionObject` elements and dispatches the remaining payload into array decoding.
source.value_from: The exact staged PoC is `17 00 D6 01 00 00 00 03 20 20 01 00 00 00 20 01`. After the harness consumes `17 00` as little-endian `typeIndex = 23` (`UA_TYPES_VARIANT`), the next byte `0xD6` has the array bit set and low six bits `0x16`, so `typeIndex == UA_TYPES_EXTENSIONOBJECT`; the following little-endian Int32 `01 00 00 00` makes the outer array length 1.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: ASan sink. Cleanup of the partially decoded `ExtensionObject` reaches `String_deleteMembers` on the aliased `NodeId` string and passes the same 1-byte heap region to `UA_free()` a second time.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `attempting double-free` at `String_deleteMembers /src/open62541/src/ua_types.c:91:5`, and the same trace identifies the previously freed region as the 1-byte `NodeId` string allocated during `NodeId_decodeBinary`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. In the unknown-type `ExtensionObject` path, the decoded `NodeId` is shallow-copied into the destination instead of being duplicated or ownership-transferred. `ExtensionObject_decodeBinary()` later frees `binTypeId`, so `dst->content.encoded.typeId` becomes a dangling alias. The fix replaces this assignment with `UA_NodeId_copy(typeId, &dst->content.encoded.typeId);`.

tainted_value_origin.description: Allocation site of the eventual double-free target. During `NodeId_decodeBinary()`'s string case, `String_decodeBinary()` reaches this call with `length = 1` and allocates the 1-byte buffer later aliased into `dst->content.encoded.typeId` and freed twice.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The sole `ExtensionObject` element contributes the `NodeId` bytes `03 20 20 01 00 00 00 20`: string-encoding `0x03`, namespaceIndex `0x2020`, string length `1`, and one identifier byte `0x20`.

parser_admitted.description: After the harness chooses `UA_TYPES_VARIANT`, the top-level `Variant` header admits the payload as an array of `ExtensionObject` elements and enters recursive element decoding.

unknown_type_arm.description: The sole element's decoded `NodeId` is not a numeric binary-encoding id, so the decoder keeps the `ExtensionObject` in encoded form instead of decoding typed content.

fine_trace.code:
uint16_t typeIndex = (uint16_t)(data[0] | data[1] << 8);
UA_StatusCode ret = UA_decodeBinary(&binary, newOffset, dst, &UA_TYPES[typeIndex], 0, nullptr);
fine_trace.note: Harness step. The staged PoC starts with `17 00`, so `typeIndex = 23` (`UA_TYPES_VARIANT`). The remaining 14 bytes are wrapped as `binary` and forwarded unchanged to the project decoder.

Source. The top-level `Variant` header byte `0xD6` selects `UA_TYPES_EXTENSIONOBJECT` as the element type and sets the array bit, so the remaining payload is decoded as a one-element `ExtensionObject` array.
For the sole array element, the next bytes `03 20 20 01 00 00 00 20` materialize `binTypeId` as a string `NodeId` with namespaceIndex `0x2020`, string length 1, and identifier byte `0x20`.
Inside `NodeId_decodeBinary()`'s string case, `String_decodeBinary()` reaches this allocation with `length = 1` and creates the 1-byte heap buffer that becomes the eventual double-free target.
Because the decoded `NodeId` is a string identifier rather than a numeric binary-encoding id, `UA_findDataTypeByBinary()` returns `NULL` and the decoder takes the unknown-type branch.

Root-cause transition. The unknown-type path stores the decoded `NodeId` in encoded form, but it does so by shallow-copying `*typeId`. `dst->content.encoded.typeId.identifier.string.data` now aliases the same 1-byte buffer still owned by `binTypeId`.

The final witness byte `0x01` sets `encoding == UA_EXTENSIONOBJECT_ENCODED_BYTESTRING`, but the file ends before the required 4-byte encoded-body length, so `ExtensionObject_decodeBinaryContent()` returns a decode error. `ExtensionObject_decodeBinary()` still deletes `binTypeId`, which frees the aliased 1-byte string once and leaves `dst->content.encoded.typeId` dangling.
Because decoding the sole `ExtensionObject` element returned non-GOOD, the outer array decoder immediately cleans up the one already initialized array slot.
Cleanup of that partially decoded element takes the encoded-`ExtensionObject` branch and forwards the stale `content.encoded.typeId` alias to `NodeId_deleteMembers()` for a second deletion attempt.
Sink. `NodeId_deleteMembers()` reaches `String_deleteMembers()` on the aliased 1-byte string buffer from step 4 and frees it again, matching the saved AddressSanitizer double-free.

allocation_context.note: ASan's allocation stack reaches this `UA_calloc(length, type->memSize)` through `String_decodeBinary` -> `ByteString_decodeBinary` -> `NodeId_decodeBinary` while materializing the string `NodeId`.

free_context.note: The previous-free stack corresponds to the `UA_NodeId_deleteMembers(&binTypeId)` call after `ExtensionObject_decodeBinaryContent()`. The ASan frame line map reports `ExtensionObject_decodeBinary:977`, but the staged vulnerable source places this unconditional free for the BYTESTRING branch at line 983.

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch replaces `dst->content.encoded.typeId = *typeId;` with `UA_NodeId_copy(typeId, &dst->content.encoded.typeId);`, which directly fixes the aliasing root cause. Stage 02 does not execute fixed-version validation, so `patch_resolves` remains false here.

format.contract: The exact 16-byte binary blob `17 00 D6 01 00 00 00 03 20 20 01 00 00 00 20 01`. Interpreted by `fuzz_binary_decode`, `17 00` is the little-endian type selector `UA_TYPES_VARIANT`; `0xD6` is the top-level `Variant` header; `01 00 00 00` is the outer array length 1; `03 20 20 01 00 00 00 20` is a string `NodeId` with namespaceIndex `0x2020`, string length 1, and identifier byte `0x20`; and the final `0x01` is the `ExtensionObject` encoding byte with no following 4-byte body length. No broader input class is asserted.
